validity_findings.finding: Parameterized mechanism count reduction 3 vs 5 (40%, ratio 0.6) conflates GET and PUT methods for fetch_posts intent. _is_metadata_path excludes 'method', so GET and PUT observations with same intent are grouped and distilled to a single GET template (action_template.method=GET). Literal baseline counts GET /posts/{id} and PUT /posts/{id} as distinct (method matters), but parameterized kernel discards PUT distinction — template would execute GET for PUT tasks, which would be a semantic failure if method matters. Report attributes sharing to 'method is metadata' but spec positive_control describes 5 endpoints with distinct POST/PUT methods. Reduction therefore overstates product-relevant saving.

POST /posts, PUT /posts/{id}) ... 3 mechanisms (posts/{id} shared by GET/PUT)'
validity_findings.impact: Arithmetic 5->3 (40%) reproduces, but semantic validity requires method-aware counting or explicit declaration that method is out of scope. True method-aware parameterized count would be 3 if POST requires literal (create_post fails) plus distinct fetch_posts GET vs PUT? If method preserved, parameterized would be 4 vs 5 (20% reduction, still passes 20% threshold but at boundary). Claim ceiling must note method-excluded counting.
